question: In India, the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act was enacted in _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1951**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Industries (Development and Regulation) Act was enacted in **1951** to regulate and develop industries in India.
 
• The Act provides the central government with the authority to take necessary steps for the development and regulation of industries.
 
• It aims to ensure balanced industrial development and prevent the concentration of economic power.
 
• The Act covers a wide range of industries and requires them to obtain licenses for operation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951**

 
 
• The Act was passed by the Parliament of India in 1951 to provide for the development and regulation of certain industries.
 
• It aims to control and regulate the pattern of industrial development and the licensing of industries.
 
• The Act grants the central government the power to make rules and regulations for the registration and licensing of industrial undertakings.
 
• It also provides for the establishment of advisory bodies to assist in the administration of the Act.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of the Act**
 
 
• To ensure a balanced and coordinated development of industries.
 
• To prevent the concentration of economic power in the hands of a few individuals or groups.
 
• To regulate the location of industries for the balanced regional development.
 
• To ensure the optimal utilization of national resources for industrial development.
 
 
 
• **Licensing Provisions**
 
 
• The Act mandates that certain industries must obtain licenses from the central government before commencing operations.
 
• Licenses are granted based on criteria such as location, technical feasibility, and financial soundness.
 
• The Act also provides for the revocation of licenses in cases of non-compliance with the terms and conditions.
